summary: Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1965 to 1974. He later served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University from circa 1979 to 2017.

Masato Kobayashi is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona. From circa 2000 to 2003, he was a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Masatoshi Konishi was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1957 to 1967. He later held an academic post at Rikkyo University from circa 1974 to 2004.
Masatoshi Nagatomi was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and Harvard University. He served as a professor at Harvard University from around 1969 to 1996.

Masayuki Taira, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history, studied at Kyoto University. He held positions at Kansai University (circa 1984–1994), Osaka University (circa 1994–2016), and Kyoto Tachibana University (around 2016).

Masumi Mochizuki is a Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Minobusan University, serving as a lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies as attested in 2001 and as a professor as attested in 2015.

Mathieu Boisvert is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. Since 1992, he has served as a professor at Université du Québec à Montréal.
Matthew B. Orsborn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Guang Xing and Y. Karunadasa, and studied under traditional teachers Hsing Yun and Huishang.

Matthew Immergut, a scholar of religious studies and sociology who studied under Culadasa, served as an associate professor of sociology at the State University of New York at Purchase as attested in 2011.

Matthew King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Toronto by 2014 under Frances Garrett, having also studied under Thupten Champa and Khenpo Kunga Sherab.

Matthew R. Sayers is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel Peter Brereton and Patrick Olivelle. He held a post at Lebanon Valley College as attested in 2013.

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned an MA at the University of Hawaii and a PhD at Duke University under Richard M. Jaffe, also studying at Osaka City University and the IUC.

Matthew T. Kapstein is a Tibetologist and philosopher who earned his PhD from Brown University. He held posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University (~1990–1999), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2002–2018).

Matthias von Lexer was a linguist who studied under Albrecht Weber. He held academic posts at the University of Freiburg (~1864–1868), Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1868–1874), and the University of Würzburg (~1874–1892).

Matthieu Ricard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the Pasteur Institute under François Jacob and later studied under traditional teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche from circa 1979 to 1991.

Mattia Salvini is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his PhD from SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski. He held posts at the International Buddhist College (~2008–2011) and Mahidol University (~2011–2020).

Mauli Chand Prasad is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna. In 1984, he was attested as a lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Maurice Bloomfield was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Johns Hopkins University under Charles Rockwell Lanman, having also studied under William Dwight Whitney. In 1881, he was appointed professor at Johns Hopkins University.
Maurice O'Connell Walshe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Walpola Rahula. He held a post at the Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies from circa 1955 to 1978.
Maurice Wiles was a religious studies scholar who was educated at Tonbridge School (~1937–1941) and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1945–1949).
